definitions.explanation: A book or document that has been copied by hand, especially before the invention of printing. An important concept in the study of classical literature, historical documents, and religious texts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{貴重|きちょう}→貴重：00223_kichou⟧な{写本|しゃほん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{発見|はっけん}→発見：00085_hakken⟧⟦された→する：00392_suru⟧。
{源氏物語|げんじものがたり}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{多|おお}く⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{写本|しゃほん}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{伝|つた}わっている→伝わる：01961_tsutawaru⟧。
examples.english: Many manuscript copies of The Tale of Genji have been passed down.

examples.japanese: {写本|しゃほん}ごと⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{異|こと}なる→異なる：02101_kotonaru⟧⟦{字句|じく}→字句：12254_jiku⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦あり→ある：00006_aru⟧、⟦どれ→どれ：00547_dore⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{原文|げんぶん}→原文：20563_genbun⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{近|ちか}い→近い：00530_chikai⟧⟦か→か：09473_ka⟧⟦{研究|けんきゅう}→研究：01396_kenkyuu⟧⟦されている→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: Each manuscript has different wording, and scholars are studying which is closest to the original text.

notes:
An important term in Japanese literary studies and history. Before printing technology spread in Japan, all books were hand-copied, and the study of manuscript variations is a major field in classical literature research. The {源氏物語|げんじものがたり} alone has dozens of distinct manuscript lineages.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {写本|しゃほん}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧{書写|しょしゃ}⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to copy a manuscript by hand
- {写本|しゃほん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{伝来|でんらい}→伝来：11682_denrai⟧: the transmission of manuscripts
- {写本|しゃほん}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{異同|いどう}→異同：22569_idou⟧: textual variants between manuscripts
- {古写本|こしゃほん}: old manuscript

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{原本|げんぽん}→原本：15697_genpon⟧: the original text or document
- {版本|はんぽん}: printed book — made from woodblocks or movable type
- ⟦{古文書|こもんじょ}→古文書：15839_komonjo⟧: historical document — broader term for old documents
- {書写|しょしゃ}: copying by hand, transcription
